info.name: Customer Management System
info.description:
Full API coverage for the Customer Management System (.NET 10 / ASP.NET Core Web API — see ai_docs/api.md). Import this collection plus the companion environment file (optional — sane defaults are baked in as collection variables, so this works immediately after import even with no environment selected).

**How auth works here:** every request auto-authenticates via the collection-level Pre-request Script, which logs in once with the seeded demo merchant (`TestMerchantID` / `Merchant123`) and caches the token in collection variables until shortly before it expires. `POST /access-token` is rate-limited to 5 requests/minute, so requests deliberately do **not** each log in independently — that was the previous collection's behavior and would 429 itself out partway through a Collection Runner pass.

**Folders:**
- **Auth** — login, token verification, and invalid-credential cases.
- **Customer Lifecycle** — a numbered, top-to-bottom, self-cleaning walk through register → get → edit → deactivate → reactivate → deactivate → audit log → delete → confirm-gone. Safe to run repeatedly (Collection Runner-friendly): each pass creates and then deletes its own randomly-generated customer.
- **Customer Queries** — paginated/sortable/searchable listing and CSV export.
- **Audit Log** — the global (cross-customer) audit trail, plus the destructive clear-all-logs action.
- **Products & Purchases** — the product catalogue, recording a purchase, a customer's purchase history and a product's buyers; self-cleaning (registers and deletes its own helper customer). Consumes one unit of product stock per run.
- **Negative & Edge Cases** — validation failures (`400`), not-found (`404`), lifecycle-guardrail conflicts (`409`), and missing-auth (`401`), matching the status-code conventions documented in ai_docs/api.md and ai_docs/database.md. A few of these register their own short-lived helper customers first (same pattern as the Lifecycle folder) and, in two cases, deliberately leave a small amount of harmless demo data behind rather than adding extra cleanup requests — the same tradeoff the app's own "add test customers" bulk generator makes.
- **Health** — the unauthenticated `/health` liveness check.

See `ai_docs/index.md` for the full architecture and `ai_docs/api.md` / `ai_docs/database.md` for the validation rules and status-code conventions this collection exercises.

item.name: Auth

request.description:
Issues a JWT for the seeded demo merchant (`TestMerchantID` / `Merchant123`, see ai_docs/build-and-run.md). You normally never need to run this manually — every other request in this collection auto-authenticates via the collection-level pre-request script, which calls this same endpoint once and caches the token in collection variables until it's about to expire. Run it yourself to force an immediate refresh, e.g. after changing `merchantId`/`merchantPassword`.

Rate-limited to 5 requests/minute per client IP ([EnableRateLimiting("login")]) — exceeding it returns `429` with a small hand-written JSON body (not the usual envelope).
`[Authorize]`-gated with nothing left to do but return 200 once the JWT middleware has already validated the bearer token — see ai_docs/api.md.
Wrong password for a real merchant ID. `AuthService`/`JwtCreation` return `403`, not `401` — see ai_docs/api.md.
`AuthService.GetAccessToken` rejects empty merchant ID/password before ever touching the DB.

item.name: Customer Lifecycle

request.description:
Creates a new **active** customer with a fresh, randomly-generated name/email/MSISDN each run (built in the Pre-request Script) so this step — and the whole folder — is safe to re-run without colliding with a previous pass. The GUID is always server-generated (`Guid.NewGuid()`), never client-supplied.

Registration's response carries no `data` (mutating endpoints don't return the created row, see ai_docs/api.md's Known Gaps) — the next request looks the new customer up by the email just sent, to capture its GUID for every later step.

item.name: Customer Queries

request.description: `sortColumn` allow-list: `name`/`email`/`msisdn`. `sortDirection`: `asc`/`desc`. `pageSize` must be 1-100. `searchTerm` (disabled by default — enable it in the Params tab to try it) does a `LIKE '%...%'` match against first/last name, email and MSISDN. See ai_docs/database.md.

The one endpoint that doesn't return the JSON envelope — on success it's a raw `text/csv` file (RFC 4180, UTF-8 BOM, formula-injection-defanged), capped at 5000 rows and not limited to one page. On failure it falls back to the usual JSON envelope. See ai_docs/database.md. Open the **Save Response** > **Save to a file** option in Postman to inspect the download.

item.name: Audit Log

request.description: Newest-first across every customer (separate stored proc from the per-customer trail — see ai_docs/database.md). Rows for a since-deleted customer still show up, with `customerFirstName`/`customerLastName` as `null` rather than disappearing (no FK from the audit table to `Customer`, by design).

**Destructive — permanently wipes every audit-log row for every customer, no soft-delete (`CustomerAuditLog_DeleteAll`, a plain unconditional `DELETE`).** Carries `[Authorize(Roles = "1801")]` on top of the class-level `[Authorize]` — a no-op today since `1801` is the only role that exists, but it stops a future second role from silently inheriting access. Not wired into any other flow in this collection; run it only when you actually mean to clear the log. See ai_docs/api.md.

item.description: The global (cross-customer) audit trail and its destructive clear-all action. See ai_docs/database.md's Audit trail section.

item.name: Products & Purchases
item.description: Product catalogue and per-customer purchases (see ai_docs/products-and-purchases.md). A numbered, self-cleaning walk: register a helper customer, buy the best-stocked product, verify the purchase history and the product's buyers/sold/left numbers, check the validation and lifecycle guardrails, then delete the helper. Each run consumes one unit of stock (from whichever product has the most left), which is never restored.

item.name: Negative & Edge Cases

request.description: `CustomerRegistration.RegisterCustomerFunction` requires `firstName` — `FirstName` has no SQL-side requirement, so this check exists purely to avoid silently creating a nameless customer.
MSISDN must be 9-12 digits only (`RegexConstants.MsisdnRegex`) — no `+`, spaces or letters.
`Customer_Create`'s address parameters have no SQL-side defaults — without this check, a missing address would surface as an opaque `500` instead of a clean `400`.
